label: Five Falco households on strada Camellara
joinedWhy: On 4 MAY 1831, in act 33 of the Arienzo death register, VINCENZO FALCO of this line — thirty-eight, contadino of strada Camellara — declared the death of Michelangelo's thirteen-month-old daughter Anna and is recorded as «PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA» — a kinsman, where the other declarant, ANDREA CRISCI, fifty-eight, of the same street, is only «VICINO DELLA DEFUNTA», a neighbour. The clerk drew the distinction himself, in one sentence. The degree is not stated. Read from the image on 20 September 2026.
apartLabel: a second Michelangelo · Michele · Francesco · an older Michele — NOT joined
apartWhy:
Four more Falco households on the same short street. Nothing in any register joins them to the line or to each other. A shared surname in one small town is suggestive and is not evidence.

THE SECOND MICHELANGELO IS NEW, and he is the reason this label changed on 20 September 2026. Two Anna Falco died three years apart, each «figlia di MICHELANGELO FALCO», with two different mothers: the Anna of 4 May 1831 is MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA’s, and the Anna of 16 March 1834 is RAFFAELA FALCO’s. Both mothers were read from the image and magnified. A remarriage between them is excluded if that Mariantonia Vigliotta is the woman still bearing children to a Michele Falco in 1834, 1836 and 1842 whom he survived in 1850. So either there are two men of the name, or one of the mothers belongs to a man of the same name — and until the marriage act of December 1828 is re-read from an image, this archive will not say which.

label: Out of Paolisi — the oldest Falco claim
apartLabel: Francesco Falco, Paolisi 1714 → Arienzo 1726 — NOT joined
apartWhy: The earliest Arienzo Falco household with a stated place of origin, twelve years before Matteo's generation. It would be a satisfying answer to where the family came from. Nothing whatever joins it to this line.

label: The gentry Falco of Arienzo
apartLabel: Don Francesco Falco, proprietario · Donna Raffaela, nun — NOT joined
apartWhy: A landowner and his daughter, a nun of the Ave Gratia Plena dead at sixty-seven in 1836. Ours are contadini. Plainly a different household living elsewhere in the same town.

label: Eight Falco doors on via Orticelli
joinedWhy:
Read in one evening, 11 October 2026, from the Arienzo death registers of 1875–1882.

NUMBER 10 is where VINCENZO FALCO, generation three, died on 15 May 1875.

NUMBER 6 is where his brother MICHELE FALCO died on 28 September 1879, and where generation four died the following April — ANGELAROSA MORGILLO on the fifteenth and RAFFAELE FALCO on the twenty-first, six days apart in the same room.

NUMBER 8 is where generation three’s son GIUSEPPE FALCO died on 3 May 1882, in the room both his own sons had died in seven years earlier.

Three doors on one short lane, three generations of this line, and until that evening the archive did not know the lane mattered.
apartLabel: numbers 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 14 — six households, NOT joined
apartWhy:
Six Falco households on the same lane as the line’s own three doors, every one of them documented, dated and placed to a house number — and not one act joins any of them to the line or to each other.

NUMBER 2 and NUMBER 9: GIOVANNI FALCO, agricoltore, and GIUSEPPA MARTONE.
NUMBER 3: ANTONIO FALCO and CARMELA GUIDA, six of whose children are dead in this archive against one known to have grown up.
NUMBER 4: GIUSEPPE FALCO and NICOLETTA NUZZO, who buried a MATTEO in 1882 and named the next son Matteo in 1885.
NUMBER 10: ANTONIO FALCO and GIOVANNA MAIONE — a different Antonio, a different wife, and the number generation three died at seven years earlier.
NUMBER 14: GIUSEPPE FALCO and NUNZIA NUZZO, held apart from number 4 on one letter of a forename.
NUMBER 8: GIOACCHINO FALCO and ANDREANA CRISCI, who buried three children there — and whose wife shares a name with generation three’s wife and is demonstrably not her, since one was dead by April 1880 and the other alive that November.

A shared surname on one short street in one small town is suggestive and is not evidence.

label: A second Falco quarter on the Corso Caudino
joined: Number 58 — a daughter of the line, married out
joinedWhy: SARA FALCO, born to generation three on 19 December 1828, married ANTONIO MAURO the fruiterer on 14 February 1855 and died at fifty-eight on 22 October 1886 at Corso Caudino 58 — birth, marriage and death all three read from the register. She is on this street because of the man she married, and where a married daughter lived is a fact about her husband.
apartWhy:
A whole second cluster of the name, in a different quarter from strada Camellara, internally joined and joined to this line by nothing.

THREE OF THEM ARE BROTHERS, and that is proved by their own acts rather than guessed from the street: VINCENZO, CLEMENTE and CARMINO FALCO, each named in his own marriage act «figlio di ANGELO FALCO e di MARIA CIMMINO». They move between numbers 70, 80, 82, 83, 88 and 89 across fifteen years — the street never changes and the number will not settle.

NUMBER 77: GIOVANBATTISTA FALCO, sarto, and COSTANZA ZIMBARDO, written «Giovanni» in 1880 and «Giovanbattista» in 1884 at the same number with the same trade and the same wife.
NUMBER 57: MATTEO FALCO, dead at seventy-eight in 1880, son of GIOACCHINO FALCO and VITTORIA CIMMINO — not generation four’s father of the same name, who was eight years younger and had different parents.

The brothers’ own father, ANGELO FALCO, and his wife ANNAMARIA CIMMINO were both still alive in September 1889. Nothing read attaches any of them to this line.
